title: Переделанный салат и вечное противостояние  (The Remade Salad and the Eternal Rivalry)

segments.t: Welcome to Kukhnya Season 2, Episode 19. Max introduces the age-old rivalry between the dining room and the kitchen as an older female guest complains that her salad has too much oil. Max simply stirs the same plate and sends it back out until Chef Barinov spots the trick.
А ничего не происходит, все нормально.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Between the dining room and the kitchen.' Addressing the kitchen in the exchange, Max reaches for the Russian word "kukhni" ("kitchen", built from "kukhnya") right at the center of the line.
'Excuse me, I am listening.' Barinov casually voices this formal apology with Max using "prostite" ("forgive me") — a warmer, more earnest polite apology that literally asks someone to forgive you.
'There is far too much oil in here.' Max reacts briskly across the room, testing Barinov's reaction in the middle of the exchange.

'Please pass this along to the cooks.' Barinov briskly shares this courtesy word for Max using "pozhaluysta" ("please") — the all-purpose Russian politeness word that covers both "please" and "you're welcome".
'Have them remake the salad.' Discussing the salad around Barinov, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'They asked to have the salad remade.' Barinov responds at once in this moment, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.

'Thank you for remaking it so quickly.' Max readily uses this word of thanks in one quick breath using "spasibo" ("thank you") — the everyday word for "thank you", which grew out of the old blessing "spasi Bog" ("God save you").
'Here you go, just the way you like it.' Looking over directly around Max, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Well now, that is another matter entirely.' Max jumps in decisively beside Barinov, shifting the mood of the conversation in a single beat.
'Are you out of your mind, tell me?' Barinov answers candidly in front of Max and chooses "skazhi" ("say", from the root "skazat") so Max hears the exact meaning.
'What is going on over here?' Holding firm candidly during the talk, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
А ничего не происходит, все нормально.
'Nothing is going on, everything is fine.' Barinov responds plainly beside Max, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'I will remake it right now.' Max weighs in naturally at once and puts the weight on "peredelayu" ("will redo", from "peredelat") as the exchange unfolds.
А ничего не происходит, все нормально.

That wraps up this scene as max describes the rivalry between the dining room and the kitchen as a fussy guest sends back an oily salad, which Max pretends to remake before Chef Barinov catches him. Until next time!
